title: Anomaly orchestration playbook for token and latency spikes
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This playbook defines the operator and automation workflow for detecting, validating, and mitigating simultaneous token-burst and tail-latency anomalies affecting Redwood inference traffic. It standardizes metric definitions, dashboard queries, alert rules, automated orchestration actions, safe manual interventions, and post-incident follow-up so that incidents are resolved consistently with minimal customer impact.

Scope and intent
- Scope: all production regions and the core runtime pipeline (ingress -> inference-gateway -> router -> model-scheduler -> serving-pool -> kv-cache-proxy).
- Intent: provide a reproducible, tested procedure for handling incidents where token consumption spikes correlate with rising p95/p99 generation latency. The focus is on protecting SLOs (foreground latency and cost) while preserving customer-visible throughput.
- Not in scope: billing disputes, long-term capacity procurement, user-facing incident comms (handled by incident comms team).

Key definitions and SLOs
- Token surge: observed sustained >3x baseline token/sec for >2 minutes for a tenant or regional aggregate.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 350ms and p99 < 800ms for short-run endpoints (<=256 tokens), regional SLO error budget: 0.5% monthly.
- Critical thresholds used by this playbook:
  - token_rate_region: baseline * 3 for 2 minutes
  - p99_latency_region: >800ms for 1 minute
  - queue_depth: >250 requests queued for >30s
  - failed_responses_rate: >1% 5m window

Primary dashboards (links and queries)
- Operator > Anomaly Orchestration (canonical dashboard) — shows:
  - regional token rate heatmap (PromQL: sum(rate(inference_tokens_total[1m])) by (region))
  - per-tenant token top talkers (PromQL: sum(rate(inference_tokens_total[5m])) by (tenant_id) | topk(50, ...))
  - tail latency panel (p50/p95/p99) for short and long tails: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, region))
  - KV cache hit ratio (PromQL: sum(inference_kv_cache_hits_total) / sum(inference_kv_cache_requests_total))
  - queue length & executor utilization per GPU pool

Alerting rules (templates)
- token-surge-region (severity=high)
  - expression: increase(inference_tokens_total{region="~"}[2m]) > (region_baseline_tokens * 3)
  - for: 2m
  - runbook: trigger orchestration flow (see Automation)
- tail-latency-regional (severity=high)
  - expression: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le,region)) > 0.8
  - for: 1m
  - runbook: route to operators + automation intent check
- queue-backlog-warning (severity=medium)
  - expression: sum(inference_queue_length{region="~"}) > 250
  - for: 30s

Automation: orchestrator responsibilities
- The incident-orchestrator service (owned by eng-platform) is the canonical automation engine used by this playbook. Responsibilities:
  - validate alerts against enrichment signals (kv cache hit ratio, model-dequeue-errors, backend-oom, capacity usage)
  - apply policy-driven mitigations in order of least customer impact to most: 1) prefix cache warmup requests, 2) adaptive batching window shrink, 3) tenant soft-quota throttles, 4) model variant swap to a smaller quantized variant, 5) regional reroute to secondary capacity, 6) preempt non-critical workloads.
  - create a tactical incident channel in Slack and post summarized telemetry every 30s.

Automated mitigation sequence (default, ordered)
1) Validate and correlate: orchestrator fetches telemetry for the last 5 minutes. If token_rate and p99 both exceed thresholds and kv_cache_hit < 0.6, proceed.
2) Warmup cache: send low-cost prefix-replay requests for the top-10 active prompts via kv-cache-proxy warmup API to reduce cold KV misses. Commands: curl -X POST https://kv-cache-proxy.internal/api/v1/warmup -d '{"prompts": [...]}'.
3) Tighten batching: call /model-scheduler API to reduce target batch window from 50ms to 25ms for affected routes. CLI: redwoodctl scheduler adjust --route <route> --batch-window 25ms --reason "auto anomaly mitigation". Monitor latency impact for 2 minutes.
4) Soft-tenant-throttle: if per-tenant token contributor is in top-10 and causing >30% of token spike, apply a soft-degradation policy: evict low-priority requests (background reranks) and cap max_tokens to 256 for that tenant for 5 minutes. API: redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant <id> --max-tokens 256 --priority-filter ">=P1".
5) Model-variant fallback: if latency remains >p99 threshold and GPU pool utilization >85%, swap heavy model variant to a quantized variant (example: mixtral-8x -> mixtral-8q4a). Use safe-swap endpoint: /model-scheduler/safe-swap 
   - Safe-swap steps (automated): create canary traffic at 1% on new variant, run checksum and sample-eval set for 30s, if output regression < configured delta, promote.
6) Region reroute: if capacity constraints persist and secondary region has spare capacity, orchestrator flips regional routing policy for a subset of traffic (10% increments) with weighted routing in router service. Command: redwoodctl router reweight --from-region us-east-1 --to-region us-west-2 --weight 10
7) Evict non-critical pools: preempt background/durable jobs and best-effort tenants according to eviction-priority table (see Ownership & priorities).

Manual intervention guidance (operator checklist)
- When to step in: automation has executed step 3+ or if orchestrator fails health checks.
- Immediate manual steps:
  1) Open the incident channel and pin the canonical dashboard link.
  2) Re-run validation queries for tokens and p99 for past 10m. PromQL snippets available on dashboard tooltips.
  3) If model safe-swap is in progress and latency is not improving, abort the swap using: curl -X POST https://model-scheduler.internal/api/v1/swap/abort --data '{"swap_id":"<id>"}' and rollback to previous variant.
  4) For tenant-caused surges, contact the Solutions SRE owner (see Ownership table) and enact an immediate tenant-level soft-throttle.

Ownership & priorities
- Primary responders: Platform SRE on-call (primary) + Runtime team (secondary)
- Model-scheduler team: owner of safe-swap logic and model-variant testing (pager backfill: model-team-oncall)
- KV-cache team: owns warmup API and KV metrics
- Router team: owns region reweighting and safe fallbacks

Eviction-priority table (text)
- Priority A: interactive foreground routes, paid PLG endpoints with active sessions
- Priority B: dedicated background rerank and batch endpoints (degrade first)
- Priority C: best-effort offline ingestion and low-tier test tenants

Operator comms and escalation matrix
- Severity=high: create incident in PagerDuty, Slack channel #incident-<region>-tokens, notify Eng leadership if active customer-affecting SLO break persists >15m.
- Severity=medium: Slack channel only + post incident summary within 60m.

Example incident timeline (illustrative)
- T+0: token-surge-region alert fires (orchestrator auto-validates and posts channel).
- T+1m: orchestrator warms prefix cache and tightens batching. Slack summary posted.
- T+4m: p99 improves 30% but token rate remains; orchestrator triggers tenant soft-throttle for top offender.
- T+9m: model variant fallback scheduled and canary promoted.
- T+16m: p99 back within SLO, queue length decreasing; automation de-escalates and reverts temporary throttles after 10m cooldown.

Rollback and safety checks
- Every model-variant swap must: 1) log a swap_id, 2) run the sample-eval suite (10 predefined prompts), 3) compare tokenized outputs with baseline via fuzzy metric (BLEU-ish configured in model-scheduler). If sample-eval fails, swap is aborted and previous variant restored.
- All automated changes must be reversible with a single command. Operators must confirm the presence of swap_id and change logs in /var/log/orchestrator/change-events before proceeding.

Post-incident and retrospectives
- Postmortem owner: Platform SRE (assign within 24h). Postmortem must include timeline, root cause hypothesis, telemetry screenshots, and remediation plan with owners.
- Quality gate for playbook updates: after every major incident where automation executed step 4+, schedule a 3-day runbook review with automation, runtime, and model teams.

Testing, runbook drills, and game-days
- Quarterly: run a simulated token-surge game-day in a staging region using the synthetic traffic generator (tool: stress-gen) with the following scenario: tenant-fake-high-tokens + slow backend for 5m.
- Checklist for drills: ensure orchestrator is in dry-run mode, validate all webhook integrations to Slack/PagerDuty, run full safe-swap and verify rollback path.

Telemetry retention and diagnostics
- Short-term high-resolution telemetry: 90 days at 10s resolution for request_duration, inference_tokens_total, and queue_length.
- Long-term sampling: 1s aggregated to 1m beyond 90 days retained for 2 years.
- Diagnostic snapshots: on incident start, orchestrator will capture a 15-minute compressed snapshot and upload to artifact-store with id incident-<id>-snapshot.

Approval and change notes
- Changes to this playbook must be reviewed by: Platform SRE lead, Runtime team lead, and Product manager for API stability.
- Version note: v1.0 published 2026-01-10 by Aisha Patel. Last substantive update 2026-02-18: added safe-swap canary steps and tightened default batch-window.

Appendix: useful commands and endpoints
- redwoodctl scheduler adjust --route <route> --batch-window <ms> --reason "<text>"
- redwoodctl router reweight --from-region <A> --to-region <B> --weight <percent>
- curl -X POST https://kv-cache-proxy.internal/api/v1/warmup -d '{"prompts": ["prefix1", "prefix2"]}'
- curl -X POST https://model-scheduler.internal/api/v1/safe-swap -d '{"from":"mixtral-8x","to":"mixtral-8q4a","routes":["/v1/generate"]}'

Contact and escalation list
- Platform SRE PagerDuty: platform-sre-oncall@pagerduty.com
- Runtime team Slack: @runtime-oncall
- KV-cache owner: kv-cache-team@redwood.com
- Model-scheduler owner: modelscheduler@redwood.com

End of document
